excerpt: Rebank was a Y Combinator-backed business banking layer for startups. It has since become Caribou, a transfer pricing and international tax platform; rebanknow.com now redirects there.
content:
Rebank started as a digital banking layer for fast-growing companies. Rather than being a bank itself, it ran on top of a company's existing business bank accounts, giving finance teams one interface for their accounts and cheaper payments. In December 2019 TechCrunch reported that the Y Combinator graduate raised a $2.8 million seed round led by ADV, with Y Combinator, Oriza Ventures and angel investors including Jude Gomila. Co-founder and CEO Juan Andrade told TechCrunch that companies faced two major problems: clunky banking interfaces and unnecessarily expensive payments. Andrade had earlier built card products at the London payments company Ukash, and co-founder Simon White had been a systems engineer at Unisys and Thales.

Now Caribou. Rebank no longer operates under that name. Its old domain, rebanknow.com, now redirects to usecaribou.com, and Y Combinator's company directory says Caribou was formerly Rebank (YC Winter 2019). The founders explain on that page that building Rebank, which they describe as the first open banking product for global businesses, showed them that companies were going international earlier than law and accounting firms could keep up with. Caribou is that next product.

Caribou describes itself as transfer pricing software with the experts built in. Transfer pricing covers how related companies in a group, in different countries, charge each other. Caribou says it designs a company's transfer pricing, documents it and keeps it compliant as the business grows, so it holds up with auditors, investors and new markets. Y Combinator's page calls it an autonomous tax firm that also checks for legal risks, R&D credits and accidental tax exposure, with Juan Andrade as founder and a team based in Lisbon.

Caribou does not publish prices; its site offers a free assessment. This profile draws on Caribou's and Y Combinator's pages and published reporting. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.
